name: Oocyte/Zygote/Embryo Maturation Arrest 23

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Criteria for OOMA23

criteria.description: History of primary infertility in a woman of reproductive age, with failure to conceive after at least 12 months of unprotected intercourse.
Repeated IVF cycles showing oocyte, zygote, or embryo maturation arrest (failure to progress beyond GV, MI, or MII stage, or early embryo arrest).
Identification of pathogenic biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) variants in KIF11 by molecular genetic testing.
Exclusion of other known causes of female infertility (e.g., anatomic, endocrine, chromosomal, or other genetic causes).

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and characteristic IVF findings.

occasional.symptomName: Oocyte retrieval with no mature oocytes
Oocytes arrested at germinal vesicle (GV) or metaphase I (MI) stage

laboratory: Normal baseline hormonal profile (FSH, LH, estradiol, AMH)
imaging: Normal pelvic ultrasound (normal uterus and ovaries)
other: Oocyte maturation arrest observed during IVF cycles
No mature oocytes or early embryo arrest on embryology assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Pathogenic variants in genes other than KIF11 (e.g., TUBB8, PATL2, WEE2, etc.)
Irregular or absent menses, diminished ovarian reserve

redFlags: Repeated IVF cycle failure with oocyte or embryo maturation arrest
Absence of mature oocytes despite normal ovarian reserve and hormonal profile
references: Practice Committee of the ASRM. Diagnostic evaluation of the infertile female: a committee opinion. Fertil Steril. 2021;116(6):1532-1539.
commonPitfalls: Assuming all IVF failure is due to poor ovarian reserve or age-related factors
Overlooking genetic testing in women with repeated oocyte maturation arrest
Misattributing infertility to anatomic or endocrine causes without embryology review
Failure to distinguish between oocyte maturation arrest and fertilization failure
Not considering rare genetic etiologies in women with normal hormonal and imaging findings

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Normal FSH, LH, and estradiol levels in OOMA23
No hyperandrogenism or polycystic ovarian morphology in OOMA23

extendedDiscriminators.vsCondition: Oocyte maturation arrest due to TUBB8 mutation
extendedDiscriminators.feature: KIF11 pathogenic variants confirmed by genetic testing in OOMA23

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of biallelic pathogenic KIF11 variants on genetic testing
Presence of anatomic, endocrine, or chromosomal causes of infertility
Evidence of diminished ovarian reserve or abnormal hormonal profile
Oocyte maturation arrest not observed on IVF cycles
